questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

Don’t disturb the boy, he __prepares__ for his examination.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **is preparing**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace "**prepares**" with "**is preparing**" to correct the sentence.
 
• The sentence says, "**Don’t disturb the boy**" which means the action is happening.
 
• The **present continuous or the present progressive tense **is used to tell about whatever action is happening at the time of speaking.
 
• The structure should be: Subject + is/am/are+ v1+ ing + object__
 
• So, we have to change the tense of the sentence to make it correct.
 
• Thus, **option 2** is the correct answer.

 

**Corrected sentence**: *Don’t disturb the boy, he __is preparing __for his examination.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Prepares**: In English, the -**s **is only added to regular verbs in the present tense when the subject of the verb is a third-person singular subject.
 
• **Prepared**: Past tense of "prepare" and only used in the past tenses.
 
• **Was preparing**: "was+verb-ing" is only used in the past continuous tense to represent an action or event that was going on in the past.
 
• **Will be preparing**: "will +be+verb-ing" is only used in the future continuous tense to express action at a particular moment in the future.

• The given sentence is in the passive form and we need to change it into the active **form**.
 
• The given sentence is written in the passive form of the Simple Past Tense.
 
• The Simple Past Tense in the passive voice has the following structure: Object+ was/were V3+ by + subject__
 
• The Simple Past Tense in the active voice has the following structure: __Subject + V2+ object__
 
• Example - 
 
 
• Passive voice - *He was saved by me.*
 
• Active voice - *I saved him.*
 
 
 
• Rules of Conversion from Passive to Active Voice:
 
 
• Identify the subject, the verb, and the object.
 
• Change the object into the subject.
 
• Change the verb into the past participle form of the verb.
 
• Change the subject into an object.
 
 
 
• ​Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

 

Correct Active Voice: *The movie fascinated me.*

I had walked / for most of the day / to Kanpur and then / get on the train by Mumbai.

questions.solution:

• Replace "**get**" with "**got**" and "**by**" with "**to**" to correct the sentence.
 
• "**Had + v3**" is used in the past perfect tense to make it clear that one event happened before another in the past.
 
• In such sentences, the first action is written in the **past perfect** and second action in the **simple past** **tense**.
 
• So, "**got**" should be used here in the given sentence.
 
• The preposition **'to' **will be used instead of 'by' as it means** in the direction of**.
 
 
• Example: We went** to** Prague last year.
 
 
 
• We use "by + noun" to describe how someone travels or communicates, or how things are processed. (by car, by train etc.)
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 3** which contains an error in it.
 
• **The implied meaning of the sentence is:** I had travelled to Kanpur on foot for the majority of the day before boarding the train to Mumbai.

 

**Corrected sentence:** *I had walked for most of the day to Kanpur and then got on the train to Mumbai.*

questions.question:
**Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains a grammatical error.**

The jury was not happy with the performance / and was quite harsh. / The singer took / their criticism in heart.

options.text: The jury was not happy with the performance

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] ** __Key Points__ ** 

__
 
• The phrase "**in heart**" is not idiomatically correct.
 
• The correct phrase is "**to heart**." 
 
• 
 Collective nouns like "**jury**" are usually considered singular entities.
 
 
• 
 Therefore, the correct pronoun to use is "**its**" instead of "**their**."
 
 
• 
 In this context, "**its criticism**" is the proper usage.
 
 
• 
 The correct sentence should be "**The singer took its criticism to heart**."
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The jury was not happy with the performance and was quite harsh. The singer took its criticism to heart."* 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] ** Additional Information__ ** 

 
• **A: "The jury was not happy with the performance"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **B: "The singer took"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "and was quite harsh."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

**The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.**

P. He is well aware of the role he and his people play in keeping Shivsagar Lake beautiful and ecologically thriving.

Q. However, he is also deeply aware of the fact that the urban idea of conservation often seeks to keep traditional dwellers out.

R. Jason, 45, has a quiet, confident presence.

S. He takes a long time to open up and even after that, he speaks little.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "RSPQ"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage. 
 
• Statement R is the opening sentence of the passage as it gives a brief introduction of the person named 'Jason'.
 
• Statement S is the second sentence of the passage which explains that he takes a while to open up, and even then, he doesn't say too much.
 
• Statement P is the third sentence of the passage which explains his awareness of the contribution he and his people make to maintaining Shivsagar Lake's aesthetic appeal and ecological health.
 
• Statement Q is the last sentence of the passage which shows that he is very conscious, however, that the modern notion of conservation frequently aims to exclude traditional residents.
 
• Hence, the correct sequence is R, S, P, Q
 
• The correct answer is option 2.

 

The correct passage is: ***R**. Jason, 45, has a quiet, confident presence. **S**. He takes a long time to open up and even after that, he speaks little. **P**. He is well aware of the role he and his people play in keeping Shivsagar Lake beautiful and ecologically thriving. **Q**. However, he is also deeply aware of the fact that the urban idea of conservation often seeks to keep traditional dwellers out.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Priya assured me, “I can stay in tonight.”

options.text: Priya told me that she could stay in this night.
Priya told me that she could stay in that night.
Priya told me that she could stay in tonight.
Priya told me that she can stay in that night.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Priya told me that she could stay in that night.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is in direct speech and we need to convert it to **in****direct **speech.
 
• When we change a direct speech to an indirect speech, we must follow these rules:
 
 
• The reporting verb "**assured**" is changed to "**told**" in the indirect speech.
 
• The inverted commas ("...") are replaced with the conjunction 'that' to show the indirect speech part.
 
• The comma (,) is removed in the indirect speech.
 
• The first word of the indirect speech should be in capital letters.
 
• The modal verb 'can' in direct speech changes to 'could' in indirect speech.
 
• "**Tonight**" in the direct speech changes to 'that night' in the indirect speech.
 
 
 
• Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

 

Hence, indirect speech is - *Priya told me that she could stay in that night.*

• **Discrete**: Individually separate and distinct. (अलग)
 
 
 
• So, as per the meaning of the given words "**Inflict**" is the most appropriate option.

• Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

questions.question: **Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is unfairly. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The context suggests that the leader of the UK’s psychiatrists believes the findings simplifying the issue and attributing young people's mental health problems solely to social media is not entirely justified.
 
• The word "unfairly" suggests that social media is being blamed in a way that is not right or just, fitting the context where the psychiatrist feels the conclusions are oversimplified.
 
• Words like "legitimately" and "impartially" would imply a sense of fairness or unbiased judgment, which contradicts the leader's perspective that the blame on social media is too simplistic.
 
• "Outlandish" would imply something bizarre or extremely unusual, which doesn't fit the context of discussing the validity of blaming social media.
 
• The sentence structure and context around blank number 5 indicate the need for an adverb that reflects an opinion on the fairness of the blame placed on social media, making "unfairly" the most appropriate choice.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is- Option 3 i.e. unfairly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• Legitimately means in a way that conforms to the law or to rules. It doesn't fit the context as the statement is about whether the blame is justified, not whether it's lawful.
 
• Impartially means in a way that treats all rivals or disputants equally; fairly. This option doesn't apply because the statement addresses the issue of blame being placed without considering the complexities involved.
 
• Outlandish describes something looking or sounding bizarre or unfamiliar. This option is inappropriate because the discussion is about the appropriateness of blame, not the strangeness of the findings.

 

Complete passage: *Four of the most popular forms i.e. Facebook, Twitter, Snapchat, and Instagram of social media (1) inflict__ great damage to young people’s mental health. These four platforms have a negative effect because they can __(2) exacerbate__ children’s and young people’s body image worries, and worsen bullying, sleep problems, anxiety, depression, and loneliness. The findings follow growing __(3) concern__* *among politicians, health bodies, doctors, and parents about young people suffering harm as a result of cyberbullying and social media __(4) reinforcing__* *feelings of self-loathing and leading them to commit suicide. However, the leader of the UK’s psychiatrists said these findings were too simplistic and they **__(5) unfairly__*** *blamed social media for the complex reasons why the mental health of so many young people is suffering.*
